source.title: 25 Open Questions About Vector Bundles and Their Moduli

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth projective variety, fix numerical invariants such as rank and Chern classes for which there exists a moduli space M of semistable vector bundles on X, and consider the open subset of M parametrizing stable vector bundles. For an asymptotically generically generated vector bundle E on X, its Iitaka dimension κ(E) is the dimension of the image of the stabilized Kodaira map associated to the symmetric powers of E. What geometric properties does the stratification of the stable locus of M by fixed values of κ(E) have?

evidence.quote: Fix numerical invariants, say rank and Chern classes such that there exists a moduli space M of semistable vector bundles on X. Question 1. What are the properties of the stratification of the open part of M parametrizing stable vector bundles obtained by loci of fixed Iitaka dimension?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth projective variety with dim X > 1, and let M be a moduli space of semistable sheaves with fixed numerical invariants. In the properly semistable locus, points can correspond to sheaves that are not locally free. What is the best extension of the notion of Iitaka dimension from vector bundles to these properly semistable, possibly non-locally-free sheaves?
accepted.context_brief: Extending Iitaka dimension to semistable sheaves

evidence.quote: Question 2. If dim X > 1, then in the properly semistable part of M there are points associated to non-locally free sheaves. What is the optimal adaptation of the definition of Iitaka dimension to this more general situation?

accepted.question_text: Assume Question 2 is resolved so that Iitaka dimension is defined for properly semistable sheaves on a smooth projective variety X. Let M be the moduli space of semistable sheaves with fixed numerical invariants, and consider the subset parametrizing S-equivalence classes of properly semistable sheaves on X. What geometric features does the stratification of that subset by fixed Iitaka dimension have?
accepted.context_brief: Iitaka strata for properly semistable sheaves

evidence.quote: Then, once Question 2 has been solved, in the same spirit of Question 1, we ask: Question 3. What are the geometric features of the stratification of the subset of M parametrizing equivalence classes of properly semistable sheaves on X obtained by loci of fixed Iitaka dimension?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a normal projective variety X that admits no Ulrich sheaf?
accepted.context_brief: Existence of normal varieties without Ulrich sheaves

evidence.quote: Question 4. Does there exist a normal variety X without Ulrich sheaves?

accepted.question_text: Which smooth projective varieties admit Ulrich bundles? Equivalently, for which smooth projective varieties can one find a vector bundle satisfying the standard Ulrich vanishing and linear-resolution conditions?
accepted.context_brief: Existence of Ulrich bundles on smooth varieties

evidence.quote: Our question in this topic is: Question 5. Which smooth projective varieties carry Ulrich bundles?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth connected n-dimensional manifold with n ≥ 2 such that h^i(O_X)=0 for 1 ≤ i ≤ n−1, and let A(X) be the set of ample line bundles L on X for which h^i(L^⊗t)=0 for all integers t and all 1 ≤ i ≤ n−1. Under what conditions is A(X) nonempty, and what is the dimension of A(X)?

evidence.quote: Notation 2.6. Let X be a smooth and connected n-dimensional manifold with n ≥ 2 such that h^i(OX) = 0 for all i = 1, . . . , n − 1. We denote by A(X) the set of all ample lines bundles L on X satisfying h^i(L^⊗t) = 0 for all t ∈ Z and all i = 1, . . . , n − 1. Question 6. Under what conditions is A(X) nonempty? What is dim A(X)?

accepted.question_text: Fix a positive integer r. Let A(X) be as in Question 6, and define A(X,r) to be the set of rank-r vector bundles E on X such that h^i(E ⊗ L^⊗t)=0 for all integers t, all 1 ≤ i ≤ n−1, and every ample line bundle L in A(X). What properties characterize the subset A(X,r)?

evidence.quote: Question 7. What are the properties of the subset A(X, r) of all rank r vector bundles E on X such that h^i(E ⊗ L^⊗t) = 0 for all t ∈ Z, all i = 1, . . . , n − 1 and all L ∈ A(X)?

accepted.question_text: Let X be an n-dimensional complex manifold and fix k ≥ 1. A vector bundle E is weakly k-Buchsbaum with respect to a line bundle L if, for each t ∈ N, the multiplication map H^0(L^⊗k) ⊗ H^0(E ⊗ L^⊗t) → H^0(E ⊗ L^⊗(t+k)) has maximal rank, and similarly with respect to a subset Σ ⊆ A(X) if this holds for every L in Σ. What properties characterize the weakly k-Buchsbaum vector bundles on X?

evidence.quote: Question 8. What properties characterize the set of all weakly k-Buchsbaum vector bundles on a n-dimensional complex manifold X?

Definition 2.7 A vector bundle E is said to be weakly k-Buchsbaum with respect to a line bundle L, if for each t ∈ N the evaluation map H0(L^⊗k) ⊗ H0(E ⊗ L^⊗t) → H0(E ⊗ L^⊗(t+k)) has maximal rank, i.e. it is either injective or surjective.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a complex projective manifold of dimension greater than one. Instead of a single Higgs field E → E ⊗ Ω_X^1 or a single coHiggs field E → E ⊗ T_X, consider r ≥ 2 such fields on the same vector bundle E, with an appropriate integrability condition such as f_i ∧ f_j = 0 for all i,j. What is the optimal extension of the notions of Higgs bundle and coHiggs bundle to this multi-field setting?

evidence.quote: Question 9. What are the optimal extensions of the concepts of Higgs and coHiggs bundles to include r fields in place of 1 in the case of manifolds of dimension greater than one?
We prefer the strongest one: impose that fi ∧ fj = 0 for all i, j.

accepted.question_text: Let X = P^{n1} × ··· × P^{nk} with k ≥ 2. For low-rank coHiggs bundles on X, how does the moduli space change when one changes the polarization on X?
accepted.context_brief: Polarization dependence of coHiggs moduli on multiprojective spaces

evidence.quote: Question 10. How is the moduli space of low rank coHiggs bundles on X affected by a change of polarization?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth connected projective curve. What relationship links the Brill-Noether theory of line bundles on X to the Brill-Noether theory of stable vector bundles of rank r ≥ 2 on X, including nonemptiness, dimension, irreducibility, and related geometric behavior of the corresponding loci?
accepted.context_brief: Comparing rank-1 and higher-rank Brill-Noether theory

evidence.quote: Question 11. What is the relation between the Brill–Noether theory for line bundles on X and the Brill–Noether theory for stable rank r ≥ 2 vector bundles on X?

accepted.question_text: Fix rank r = 2 and a curve of high genus. What is the relationship between Brill-Noether loci and the loci on which the Clifford index is fixed for semistable rank-2 vector bundles?

evidence.quote: Question 12. Fix rank r = 2 and high genus. What is the relation between the Brill–Noether loci and the loci of fixed Clifford indices?

accepted.question_text: For genus-2 curves and fixed numerical data of a holomorphic triple T = (E1, E2, f), determine the wall-crossing picture for α-stability: what is the configuration of walls given by the critical values α_i, and what are the limiting moduli spaces as α → 0^+ and α → +∞?
accepted.context_brief: Wall-crossing for holomorphic triples on genus-2 curves

evidence.quote: Question 13. What is the configuration of walls and what are the limits to +∞ and to 0+ for genus 2 curves? (it should not depend on the genus 2 curve).
Let T (X, r1, r2, d1, d2, α) denote the set of (equivalence classes of) holomorphic triples with ranks r1, r2 and degrees d1, d2.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a reducible, reduced, connected projective curve. Under what assumptions on X, the rank, the polarization, and related numerical data does Butler's semistability question for the kernel bundle M_{E,V} admit a positive answer in the reducible-curve setting?

evidence.quote: Question 14. What assumptions in the case of a reducible curve imply a positive answer to Butler’s question?

accepted.question_text: For a vector bundle or sheaf near a contractible subvariety Y of a variety X, what axioms should a general theory of local characteristic classes satisfy?

evidence.quote: Question 15. What should be the axioms for a general theory of local characteristic classes of vector bundles around a contractible subvariety?

accepted.question_text: After choosing a specific local numerical invariant for a vector bundle near a contractible subvariety, what numerical values are admissible for that invariant, for example in terms of the restriction of the bundle to the subvariety?

evidence.quote: Question 16. What are its admissible numerical values?
That is, one wants to have bounds for the invariant in terms of the restriction of E to Y.

accepted.question_text: For a chosen local numerical invariant of vector bundles near a contractible subvariety, which of the admissible values are actually realized by some vector bundle?
accepted.context_brief: Existence for admissible local invariant values

evidence.quote: Question 17. Which admissible values of the local invariant are realized by some vector bundle?

accepted.question_text: For a neighborhood N of a contractible subvariety and fixed local numerical invariants, what is the moduli space of vector bundles on N having those prescribed local invariants?
accepted.context_brief: Moduli with fixed local numerical invariants

evidence.quote: Question 18. What is the moduli space of all vector bundles on N with prescribed local numerical invariants?

accepted.question_text: Let Z_k = Tot(O_{P^1}(-k)). Suppose (w,h) is a pair of admissible local numerical invariants satisfying the bounds of [BGK2, Cor. 2.18], where w and h are the width and height components of the local holomorphic Euler characteristic. Does there exist a vector bundle E on Z_k with (w(E), h(E)) = (w,h)?
accepted.context_brief: Realizing admissible width-height pairs on Z_k

evidence.quote: Question 19. Let (w, h) be admissible values of local invariants on Zk, that is, they satisfy the bounds of [BGK2, Cor. 2.18]. Does there exist a vector bundle E on Zk with (w(E), h(E)) = (w, h)?

accepted.question_text: Let W_k denote one of the local Calabi-Yau threefolds O_{P^1}(-1)⊕O_{P^1}(-1), O_{P^1}(-2)⊕O_{P^1}(0), or O_{P^1}(-3)⊕O_{P^1}(1). Which local numerical invariants stratify the moduli of holomorphic vector bundles on W_k, for k ≥ 1, into Hausdorff components in the analytic topology?
accepted.context_brief: Hausdorff stratifying invariants on local Calabi-Yau threefolds

evidence.quote: Question 20. What local invariants stratify the moduli of holomorphic vector bundles on Wk for k ≥ 1 into Hausdorff components (in the analytic topology)?

Contraction of a rational curve ℓ on a Calabi–Yau threefold W may occur in 3 cases [Ji], namely Nℓ/W must be isomorphic to one of (5.3) W1 := OP1 (−1) ⊕ OP1 (−1) , W2 := OP1 (−2) ⊕ OP1 (0) , or W3 := OP1 (−3) ⊕ OP1 (+1) . Let us denote by Wk any of the previous Calabi–Yau threefolds in (5.3).

accepted.question_text: After identifying suitable local invariants for W_k, construct a Hausdorff stratification of the moduli stack M_n(W_k) of holomorphic vector bundles E on W_k with local holomorphic Euler characteristic χ(ℓ,E)=n.

evidence.quote: Question 21. Construct a Hausdorff stratification of the moduli stack Mn(Wk) of holomorphic bundles on Wk with χ(ℓ, E) = n.

accepted.question_text: For rank-2 vector bundles E on W1, is every admissible value of h^1(W1, End(E)) realized by some vector bundle E?

evidence.quote: Question 22. Is every admissible value of h^1(W1, End(E)) realized by some vector bundle E?

accepted.question_text: Is the Atiyah-Jones conjecture true for every irrational complex surface, i.e. does the inclusion of the instanton moduli space of charge k into the corresponding gauge-theoretic configuration space induce isomorphisms in low-degree homology and homotopy in that setting?

evidence.quote: Question 23. Is the Atiyah–Jones conjecture true for any irrational complex surface?
Conjecture 6.1 (Generalized Atiyah–Jones conjecture). Let X be a 4-dimensional real manifold. Then the inclusion θk : Mk → Bk induces isomorphisms in homology and homotopy...

accepted.question_text: Does the vanishing result analogous to Theorem 6.2, which compares the homology of the moduli space of rank-2 vector bundles with that of the irreducible component of the corresponding moduli stack for large c_2, extend from products of Pic-independent curves to every surface of general type?

evidence.quote: Question 24. Does a generalization of Thm. 6.2 holds for any surface of general type?
Theorem 6.2. [BGRS, Thm. 18] Assume c2 >> 0, and let Σ1, Σ2 be Pic-independent smooth projective curves. Then, for q < c2 we have Hq(Mc2(Σ1 × Σ2),Msc2(Σ1 × Σ2)) = 0.

accepted.question_text: For a complex surface X, what is the fundamental group of the moduli space of instantons on X, or equivalently of the corresponding moduli space of holomorphic vector bundles when the Kobayashi-Hitchin correspondence applies?
accepted.context_brief: Fundamental groups of instanton and bundle moduli

evidence.quote: Question 25. What is the fundamental group of the moduli space of instantons (or holomorphic bundles) on X?
